answer: Weakly to moderately, and only as a rank signal. Across 136 non-interior marks with a depth (of 159; 7 lack depth, 16 flagged interior), Spearman rho between DEM sink depth (Fill minus DEM, 2 m 3DEP) and surveyed height above ground is 0.35 at the mark cell (95% bootstrap CI 0.18-0.51) and 0.37 using the max sink within 5 m (r2 about 0.15). Sink depth separates marks from random control points within 500 m (AUC 0.75; 54% of marks vs 12% of controls have sink >0.15 m), but 35% of marks sit on cells with zero sink. It is not a calibrated depth predictor: slope is about 0.18 m of flood per m of sink, and sink magnitudes (mean 0.9 m within 10 m) exceed observed depths (mean 0.57 m). Fit is best in Richmond and the Bronx (rho 0.5-0.6) and poor in Queens and Kings (about 0.25-0.3).
traps_or_caveats: CSV line 1 is a citation; header parsed from line 2.
Units: depths in ft converted to m (x0.3048); sanity check of surveyed ground (elev_ft minus height_above_gnd) vs DEM gives median difference 0.02 m, so datum and units are consistent.

Concept mismatch: sink depth is ponding depth in a closed DEM depression; the mark is height of a water line on a wall/object. Ida flooding was mostly rapid sewer-overwhelmed/overland flow, so sinks are not a physical predictor of depth; correlation is a proxy only.
Marks exist only where flooding occurred; no true non-flood sites. Controls are random points within 500 m (some may have flooded), so AUC is indicative only.

Interior marks: 16 flagged by strict keywords (basement/inside/hallway etc.); the case file's looser regex also catches garages and 'outside of basement door' (31 hits), so flagging is imprecise. Results are similar excluding either set.
11 marks have height 0 and 7 have none; zero-depth marks excluded in a sensitivity run (rho 0.29).

Bare-earth DEM omits sewers, buildings, curbs; buildings are interpolated ground so sinks at walls are unreliable. Phone/Car GPS horizontal accuracy is coarse (several m), hence the 5 m-radius sensitivity; DEM is a bilinear 2 m export, not native lidar.

Fill is run per tile, so tile edges are treated as outlets; no mark within 100 m of an edge was affected. Marks are clustered at sites (spatially autocorrelated) so the CI is optimistic; n small per county (NY County n=6).
Max-in-radius sink is biased upward relative to point sink; no Score My Layer run was done because this is a continuous depth-vs-depth correlation, not a catalog prediction.
